output.reason: Two days of runny nose and mild sore throat with fever denied and intake maintained is consistent with a self-limited upper respiratory illness, and no reported feature requires clinician assessment, prescribing or testing now.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now: rest, fluids, and comfort measures such as saline nasal rinses or throat lozenges. Two days of runny nose and mild sore throat with no fever and normal eating and drinking usually settles on its own. Seek same-day care if you develop trouble breathing or swallowing, drooling, severe one-sided throat pain, neck swelling or stiffness, fever, or if symptoms worsen or last beyond about 10 days.

Severe or one-sided throat pain, neck swelling or stiffness
